part3.title: Part 3 – Complete the Story
part3.instruction: Read the story. Choose a word from the box. Write the correct word next to numbers 1–10. There is one example.
part3.storyText: Jane loves reading about different animals in her school [example: library]. Last Friday, Jane's (1) ________ told the class to find interesting (2) ________ of wild animals on the computer. 'Look on the animal (3) ________ I told you about yesterday,' she said. 'Work with a friend. Choose a really strong animal but talk about your different (4) ________ first before writing.' Jane worked with Paul. 'Bears are great,' Paul said. 'Let's find a picture of a bear in a cold river. They're really good at catching fish! Or a lion? People are (5) ________ of those because of their loud roar. Let me show you a picture of a lion with its mouth open!' 'What about kangaroos?' Jane said. 'They have longer and much (6) ________ tails than bears or lions. It's their powerful tails that make them really good at (7) ________ across grasslands! Their back legs are the strongest, too.' Paul looked at Jane in admiration. 'OK! You're right again, Jane!' he said. 'You're the (8) ________ girl in our class!' Then Jane took out a notebook and carefully wrote down the website (9) ________ so she could show her parents at home. Her parents were very (10) ________ when they saw how far kangaroos could jump!

part4.title: Part 4 – Factual Text
part4.instruction: Read the text. Choose the right words and write them on the lines.
paragraphs: Dolphins are part of the whale family. They are smaller (1) ________ most whales and they have small, sharp teeth.
Dolphins are very clever animals. They learn things very (2) ________ and a dolphin can make noises to 'talk' to another dolphin in its pod.
Dolphins live with their families in the ocean. They like to play in the water and to jump (3) ________ of the water and splash back in again.
A lot of people (4) ________ sail boats say that dolphins like to be near people. They come very near to boats and sometimes they (5) ________ alongside the boats for days.
Scientists spend a lot of time studying how dolphins communicate. They have found that dolphins have special clicks (6) ________ call each other by name.
Dolphins must come up to the surface of the sea to breathe air through a blowhole. They (7) ________ swim very fast when they are hunting fish.
When dolphins sleep, only half of (8) ________ brain rests at a time. This keeps them safe from predators (9) ________ allows them to keep breathing while sleeping.
Many children love dolphins because they are (10) ________ friendly and playful animals in the ocean.

part5.title: Part 5 – Complete Sentences about the Story
part5.instruction: Look at the pictures and read the story. Write 1, 2 or 3 words to complete the sentences about the story.

storyPassages.text: Daisy's family lived in a flat in the city, but every weekend they drove to the countryside to see Daisy's grandparents. They lived on a large farm. In the car, last Saturday, the family talked about the farm. 'It's so quiet there!' Daisy's mum said happily. 'I like working outside in the fresh air!' her father said. 'I love helping Grandpa with all the farm animals,' Daisy said with a smile. 'Look! Here we are at last!'

They were surprised when they saw six noisy trucks parked on the farm. And when they got out of the car, it started to rain heavily. It was cold, too. 'Oh dear!' Daisy's mum said. 'It's very noisy here today with all those trucks.' 'And I can't work outside in this heavy rain,' Daisy's father said. 'Well, you two can sit inside and have tea with Grandma,' said Daisy. 'But I have to go out and help Grandpa feed the cows and wash the sheep!'

Daisy worked all afternoon in the cold, wet weather without complaining. She gave the hungry cows their dry grass, carefully washed some sheep and carried heavy baskets of fresh vegetables. After dinner, Daisy was tired but happy. 'The best farmer in your whole family isn't your dad or your mum. It's you, Daisy!' her grandfather said proudly. 'That's good because I want to be a farmer like you one day, Grandpa,' Daisy answered with a big smile!
